verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission is set to launch no earlier than April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the evening Artemis II is set to launch its NASA mission to the moon'; R4: 'Artemis II is scheduled to launch Wednesday, April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the launch date as April 1, 2026, matching the 'no earlier than' phrasing for pre-launch planning.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed mission to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'For the first time since 1972, the countdown clock... crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit'; R6: 'last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972'; R7: 'first humans back to the Moon in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm Artemis II as the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: Four astronauts will fly a 10-day mission around the Moon on Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: '10-day journey around the moon'; R5: '10-day mission'; R6: '10-day mission'; R7: '10-day mission around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly state four astronauts on a 10-day lunar flyby/orbit mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test the Orion spacecraft and its systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'test flight... testing systems'; R5: 'test the Orion spacecraft’s ability'; R7: 'test Orion’s systems'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Artemis II as a test mission for Orion and its systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed flyby of the Moon to test life support systems and navigation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'lunar flyby... test systems'; R5: 'test life support'; R7: 'test life-support... navigation systems'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches 10-day flyby and tests including life support and navigation.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman... Victor Glover, Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; identical in R5, R6, R7
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list confirmed across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will use the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft'; consistent across sources
verifications.reasoning: All sources specify SLS rocket and Orion capsule for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will fly to the far side of the Moon on Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'zoom around the far side of the moon'; R7: 'around the farside of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state flyby includes the far side.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will travel further into space than any human has ever gone on Artemis II.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'farthest that any humans have traveled from Earth: 252,799 miles'; R7: 'surpass the record... farthest humans have ever traveled'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Artemis II sets new human distance record from Earth.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will launch from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R6: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R7: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: All sources specify Kennedy Space Center, Florida as launch site.

verifications.claim: The Artemis III mission intends to land humans on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis III was originally planned as the first crewed lunar landing... revised plan for Artemis III to perform tests... in Earth orbit... no longer land on the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm original intent but explicit revision to no landing; current plan is Earth orbit tests.
